listings.title: Field Applications Engineer Intern
listings.desc:
Field Applications Engineer Intern
 Location: San Jose, California
 Employment type: U.S. internship
 Work arrangement: Fully in-office
 About the role
 As a Field Applications Engineer Intern, you will help customers and partners implement Astera Labs integrated-circuit and hardware products in real systems. You will work alongside field applications, product applications, hardware, software, validation, quality, sales, and operations teams to understand system requirements, support design-in activities, and help investigate and resolve technical issues.
 This is a hands-on opportunity to build experience across customer engineering, system-level debugging, technical communication, and product development. You will contribute to meaningful work with visible product or business impact, receive mentorship, and communicate your results to technical stakeholders.
 What you’ll do
 Learn Astera Labs products, software, and solutions and apply that knowledge to customer architectures and system requirements, including performance, workloads, software, power, thermal, and mechanical considerations.
 Support customer design-in activities, including product demonstrations, technical presentations, technical Q&A, and delivery of product and design documentation.
 Participate in customer schematic, board-layout, architecture, and system-design reviews.
 Help reproduce and understand implementation issues using system hardware details, logs, firmware and software information, operating-system details, tests, and results.
 Collaborate with product applications and other internal engineering teams to investigate issues, develop actionable solutions, and communicate next steps.
 Document customer information, debugging progress, test results, feedback, and resolution plans in Jira or related support systems.
 Assist with lab-based testing, software/firmware regressions, interoperability testing, data analysis, and technical collateral as aligned with team priorities.
 Contribute to customer-specific technical task forces and support issue transitions to the appropriate applications, engineering, or quality teams.
 Prepare clear documentation and a final presentation that explain your approach, findings, impact, and learning.
 What you bring
 Current enrollment in a bachelor’s or master’s program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.
 Strong technical fundamentals and evidence of applying them through coursework, laboratory work, research, internships, co-ops, senior design, hackathons, or personal projects.
 Interest in hardware/software systems, computer architecture, embedded systems, networking, high-performance computing, AI infrastructure, or related interconnect technologies such as PCIe or Ethernet.
 Ability to build, test, debug, analyze, and explain technical work—not simply list tools or technologies.
 Familiarity with programming or scripting, especially Python; experience with C/C++ or MATLAB is useful depending on the project.
 Systematic problem-solving skills, curiosity, attention to detail, ownership, and willingness to learn quickly.
 Clear written and verbal communication and comfort collaborating across hardware, software, validation, architecture, applications, quality, and customer teams.
 Interest in understanding customer requirements and connecting technical details to system-level outcomes.
 We value the quality, ownership, and impact of your work more than a particular school, course title, or tool list. If you meet many of the qualifications but not every item, we encourage you to apply.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. listings.desc:
Product Applications Engineer Intern (Leo)
 Location: San Jose, California
 Employment type: Internship
 Work arrangement: On-site
 About Astera Labs
 Astera Labs builds purpose-built connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI infrastructure. The Product Applications team helps translate those products into successful system deployments through technical collateral, product integration support, lab debug, validation, and cross-functional collaboration.
 Leo is Astera Labs’ CXL Smart Memory Controller product line. Leo solutions support memory expansion, pooling, and sharing for AI and cloud platforms, with capabilities including diagnostics, telemetry, and interoperability across processor and memory ecosystems.
 The opportunity
 As a Product Applications Engineer Intern, you will work with experienced applications and engineering teams to help customers and internal partners understand, integrate, validate, and debug Leo products. You will gain hands-on experience at the intersection of high-speed connectivity, memory systems, embedded firmware/software, and customer-facing product engineering.
 This is a practical engineering role for someone who enjoys moving between technical documentation, lab investigation, data and log analysis, and collaborative problem-solving. You will contribute to meaningful work that supports products used in next-generation AI infrastructure.
 What you’ll do
 Support application-level investigation of Leo product questions and issues by reviewing system and device logs, reproducing problems in lab environments, documenting findings, and coordinating next steps with engineering teams.
 Help create, update, and review product collateral such as product briefs, datasheets, application notes, integration guidance, debug documentation, and training materials.
 Support software and firmware regression testing, including executing test flows, collecting results, identifying issues, and helping track follow-up actions.
 Participate in interoperability testing with partner devices and platforms; help analyze results and prepare clear reports for internal and external use.
 Build familiarity with CXL and PCIe-based systems, DDR memory, I2C/SMBus, embedded firmware, software development kits, diagnostics, and telemetry.
 Collaborate with Product Applications, Field Applications, firmware/software, hardware, validation, product, and sales teams throughout the product lifecycle.
 Contribute to internal product training and knowledge sharing by helping prepare materials, demonstrations, or technical walkthroughs.
 Track work and issues clearly in team tools, communicate progress and blockers, and present project outcomes to technical and business stakeholders.
 What you bring
 Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
 Coursework, project, research, or hands-on experience involving computer architecture, high-speed interfaces, memory systems, embedded systems, hardware/software integration, or system validation.
 Interest in learning how semiconductor connectivity products are integrated into real server and AI infrastructure systems.
 Ability to approach technical problems methodically, use evidence from logs or measurements, and communicate findings clearly.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and a collaborative working style.
 Experience with any of the following is helpful: C/C++, Python or other scripting, Linux, CXL, PCIe, DDR/DRAM, I2C/SMBus, firmware/SDKs, Jira, or lab equipment.
 Ability to work on-site in San Jose, California, for the internship.
 Internship experience and compensation

listings.title: Product Applications Engineer Intern (Signal and Connectivity)
listings.desc:
Product Applications Intern, Signal & Connectivity (Aries/Taurus)
 Location: San Jose, California
 Employment type: Internship
 About Astera Labs
 Astera Labs is a leader in semiconductor-based connectivity solutions that enable the scalability and performance required for modern cloud and AI infrastructure. Our products help customers build high-performance, reliable systems across the data center.
 About the role
 The Product Applications Intern, Signal & Connectivity, will support product applications work across the Aries and Taurus connectivity product lines within the Signal & Connectivity Group. This role is designed for a curious, hands-on student who wants to understand how silicon, hardware, software, and customer systems come together in real-world applications.
 You will work with product applications engineers and cross-functional partners to evaluate products, investigate technical issues, support interoperability and validation activities, and turn technical findings into clear documentation. The internship offers exposure to both customer-oriented problem solving and the engineering workflows used to bring connectivity products into production.
 What you will do
 Learn the architecture, interfaces, system use cases, and application considerations for Aries and Taurus products.
 Assist with lab bring-up, product evaluation, interoperability testing, characterization, and technical debug.
 Reproduce and investigate hardware, software, firmware, and system-level issues using structured test plans and engineering data.
 Analyze logs, measurements, and test results to identify patterns, summarize findings, and recommend next steps.
 Develop or improve scripts and lightweight automation to make testing, data collection, and analysis more efficient.
 Help create and maintain application notes, test reports, debug guides, product collateral, and other technical documentation.
 Collaborate with product applications, design, firmware, validation, systems, and field-facing teams to resolve issues and support customer use cases.
 Participate in technical discussions, communicate progress clearly, and present project results to technical and non-technical audiences.
 What you bring
 Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.
 Coursework, project, laboratory, or research experience involving digital systems, computer architecture, hardware/software integration, embedded systems, or related areas.
 Interest in hands-on debugging and the ability to approach unfamiliar technical problems methodically.
 Experience with Python or another programming language for scripting, automation, or data analysis.
 Strong analytical, written, and verbal communication skills.
 Ability to work collaboratively across teams, ask thoughtful questions, and take ownership of defined projects.
 Preferred experience
 Exposure to high-speed connectivity, system interoperability, networking, or protocol-based hardware.
 Experience working with lab equipment, test automation, logs, or structured engineering data.
 Familiarity with technical documentation, issue tracking, or software repositories.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. listings.title: Applications Engineering  Intern
listings.desc:
To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
 Group/Division 
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Film and Scatterometry Technology (FaST) division delivers industry-leading metrology solutions essential to advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its portfolio includes systems for measuring film thickness, critical dimensions, composition, and resistivity—key to developing and scaling next-gen IC processes. FaST partners closely with customers from early R&D through high-volume production, ensuring performance and process alignment. 
 What You'll Do 
 In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
 We are seeking a highly motivated engineer to join our team in the development, release, and support of KLA’s Film/OCD Metrology products. This role is critical to advancing our technology and solving complex customer challenges through deep technical understanding and innovative problem-solving.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Assist in the development and release of advanced Film/OCD Metrology products.
 Develop a deep understanding of customer applications and use cases.
 Translate customer challenges into actionable problem statements.
 Design and execute data collection plans to support product development and troubleshooting.
 Analyze data and recommend corrective actions or design improvements.
 Communicate effectively through oral presentations, written reports, meeting minutes, and project summaries.
 Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering, applications, and customer support teams.
 Required Qualifications: 
 Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Excellent communication skills—both written and verbal.
 Ability to work independently and in a team environment.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Experience in semiconductor metrology or related technologies.
 Familiarity with thin film/OCD characterization techniques.
 Prior experience working with customers or in a customer-facing role.
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Working towards a college degree
 About KLA 
 We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.

listings.title: Electrical Validation Engineer Intern
listings.desc:
Electrical Validation Engineer Intern
 Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site 
 About Astera Labs
 Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our Electrical Validation teams measure, debug, and validate the electrical behavior of complex hardware platforms so products can move confidently through bring-up, validation, and release.
 The opportunity
 Join the Electrical Validation team and gain hands-on experience validating high-performance hardware. You’ll learn the team’s products, lab environment, measurement methods, firmware and update flows, and validation processes while contributing to a scoped project with a visible technical outcome.
 This internship is designed for someone who enjoys working close to the hardware: setting up an experiment, selecting the right instrument, collecting trustworthy data, analyzing the result, investigating unexpected behavior, and documenting what the team should do next. You’ll collaborate with Electrical Validation, firmware, system validation, ATE, PApps, program-management, and other engineering teams.
 What you’ll do
 Learn the Electrical Validation environment, assigned product area, lab equipment, scripts, specifications, and project success criteria.
 Run repeatable electrical measurements and validation workflows for hardware platforms, boards, links, interfaces, or subsystems.
 Set up and use lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, BERTs, VNAs, power supplies, electronic loads, temperature chambers, probes, and related fixtures under engineering guidance.
 Collect, organize, and analyze voltage, current, timing, signal-quality, link, power, temperature, or other electrical data as appropriate for the project.
 Compare results with specifications, expected behavior, previous runs, and validation criteria; identify trends, anomalies, margins, and failure conditions.
 Support hardware bring-up and debug by checking connections, configurations, firmware or update flows, test scripts, instrument settings, and environmental conditions.
 Develop or improve Python, shell, or other automation scripts for measurements, data collection, report generation, or repeatability.
 Create clear data packages, validation reports, plots, checklists, Confluence pages, and handoff documentation that others can trust and reuse.
 Investigate defined technical issues, form evidence-based hypotheses, run focused experiments, and communicate recommended next steps.
 Collaborate with firmware, system validation, ATE, PApps, design, and other cross-functional teams to unblock shared execution and close assigned tasks.
 Keep project trackers, action items, and technical documentation current while communicating progress, blockers, and risks.
 Own a scoped validation workflow or product slice with increasing independence and present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.
 What you bring
 Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or a related field.
 Foundational understanding of circuits, electronics, digital systems, signal integrity, power, measurements, or hardware interfaces.
 Interest in learning how to use laboratory instruments and how to turn measurements into reliable engineering conclusions.
 Programming or scripting experience in Python, C/C++, MATLAB, shell, or another language used for automation and data analysis.
 Comfort learning in a Linux or technical lab environment and working with specifications, logs, plots, test procedures, and source control.
 A methodical approach to troubleshooting: verify the setup, isolate variables, collect evidence, compare against expectations, and document what changed.
 Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain results and uncertainty to cross-functional partners.
 Ownership, curiosity, humility, and persistence in an environment where experiments may need to be repeated and refined.

 Role Overview 
 As a Firmware Engineering Intern on the Optical Transceiver Module or Active Electrical Cable (AEC) Firmware team, you will contribute to embedded software that helps bring up, validate, and improve high-speed connectivity products. You will work across C and Python codebases, build practical debugging skills, and collaborate with firmware, hardware, and validation engineers to turn requirements into reliable product functionality.
 This is an opportunity to apply your coursework and embedded firmware experience to real products supporting the next generation of rack-scale AI infrastructure. You will gain hands-on exposure to firmware development, lab testing, automation, and system-level problem solving while learning in a fast-moving environment where interns are encouraged to grow and make meaningful contributions.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Firmware Development 
 Implement and enhance embedded firmware in C for optical and active electrical cable products.
 Develop Python scripts and tools for test automation, device configuration, log parsing, and data analysis.
 Translate requirements into clear, maintainable code with guidance from experienced firmware engineers.
 Bring-Up, Debugging, and Validation 
 Support firmware bring-up on embedded platforms and assist with board- and system-level debugging.
 Execute functional, regression, and interoperability tests; document results and track issues.
 Use lab equipment and software tools to isolate failures, verify fixes, and improve product quality.
 Collaboration and Documentation 
 Partner with hardware, systems, and validation engineers to investigate issues and deliver integrated solutions.
 Participate in code reviews and apply feedback to improve reliability, readability, and maintainability.
 Contribute to design notes, test plans, debug reports, and other engineering documentation.
 Basic Qualifications

To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
 Group/Division 
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Film and Scatterometry Technology (FaST) division delivers industry-leading metrology solutions essential to advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its portfolio includes systems for measuring film thickness, critical dimensions, composition, and resistivity—key to developing and scaling next-gen IC processes. FaST partners closely with customers from early R&D through high-volume production, ensuring performance and process alignment. 
 What You'll Do 
 In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.

As an intern, you will work alongside experienced software engineers to design, develop, test, and support software solutions that contribute to advanced semiconductor process control and inspection systems. This internship provides hands-on experience with real-world projects, modern development tools, and cross-functional collaboration
 Responsibilities
 Participate in the design, implementation, testing, and maintenance of software applications and features.
 Develop and execute unit tests, automation scripts, and validation procedures.
 Analyze software defects, troubleshoot issues, and assist in implementing solutions.
 Collaborate with software engineers, systems engineers, and quality engineers to achieve project objectives.
 Utilize software development tools, source control systems, and CI/CD workflows.
 Document software designs, test results, and technical findings.
 Present project progress and results to engineering teams and management.
 Required Qualifications 
 Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical field.
 Expected graduation date between December 2027 and June 2029. 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Experience with one or more programming languages such as C++, C#, Python, Java, or JavaScript. 
 Understanding of software engineering fundamentals, data structures, and algorithms.
 Excellent communication and teamwork skills.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience with AI-assisted development tools.
 Exposure to AI/ML, computer vision, image processing, or data analytics. 
 Familiarity with object-oriented design, source control, and software testing.

Requires less than 1 year of related experience

 About the role
 Astera Labs is seeking a Signal Integrity Engineer Intern to join the Signal and Power Integrity (SI/PI) team. In this role, you will gain hands-on experience analyzing high-speed interconnects and supporting PCB- and system-level designs through simulation, measurement, and cross-functional engineering collaboration.
 You will work on a meaningful project with guidance from experienced engineers while building practical skills in signal-integrity analysis, lab validation, technical communication, and engineering judgment.

 Enrollment in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.
 Academic, research, or project experience with one or more of the following: high-speed digital design, signal integrity, transmission lines, electromagnetics, PCB design, differential signaling, or S-parameters.
 A foundational understanding of frequency-domain or time-domain analysis and how interconnect design affects signal quality.
 Ability to learn simulation and measurement workflows, work carefully with technical data, and communicate conclusions clearly.
 Strong ownership, curiosity, practical judgment, and willingness to collaborate across functions.
 Preferred qualifications
 Familiarity with PCB or system-level SI/PI simulation, channel analysis, or lab measurement.

To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
 Group/Division 
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Film and Scatterometry Technology (FaST) division delivers industry-leading metrology solutions essential to advanced semiconductor manufacturing.  Enthusiastic communicator to provide detailed guidance to colleagues to solve problems, and technical summaries for internal functional teams and management.
 Understanding of optical, electrical, mechanical and software systems and their interactions in the context of complex industrial equipment is a plus.

About Marvell 
 Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 
 At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 
 Your Team, Your Impact 
As an Analog IC Design Engineer with Marvell, you’ll be a member of the Central Engineering business group. If you picture Marvell as a wheel, Central Engineering is the center hub providing IP to be used by all the other spokes on that wheel, including Automotive, Storage, Security, and Networking. You’ll be part of a small analog team making a big impact on this organization. Additionally, Marvell has the perfect size and scale for you to learn several aspects of engineering that will be new to you, but also have the time and freedom to dive deep into the details of your specialization on most projects. 
 What You Can Expect 
In this (hybrid/remote/in-office) role in LOCATION, you’ll build transistor level circuits from scratch or be given existing blocks to improve or port. Using a variety of CAD tools, but primarily Cadence, you will build or improve your circuit, simulate different performance metrics and measure other parameters. You’ll do circuit analysis and if your circuit looks good, you’ll send it to layout for physical design. Once it’s created, you get it back, run simulations and tests, and continue iterating until the circuit performs precisely as you need it to.
You’ll attend weekly meetings with your team to discuss your projects at a high level. If any issues arise, the team may take a more focused look at the problem to work out a solution. You’ll also attend meetings with senior designers and managers to review your work at a detailed level. On this team, you’ll have the opportunity to see your designs go from an idea all the way through production and into use by other groups at Marvell.

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.



The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.



This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our AI, Data, and Analytics teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process.

Software-defined vehicles generate enormous amounts of data, from vehicle telemetry to manufacturing and fleet operations.  - Design, build, or maintain data pipelines, analytics workflows, or ML supporting infrastructure

 - Write Python and SQL code to process, transform, and validate data

 - Contribute to automated testing for data quality and pipeline reliability

 - Document your work and share progress with your team throughout the internship


QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum:

Preferred:

listings.desc:
This posting supports current and anticipated early-career hiring needs. Applying allows our recruiting team to consider you for opportunities that align with your qualifications, preferences, and availability. An immediate opening or interview is not guaranteed. 
 Where are these roles located?  You’ll have the opportunity to work with teams in:
 Colorado Springs, Colorado
 Irvine, California
 Longmont, Colorado
 Fremont, California
 Rochester, Minnesota
 San Jose, California
 System Tools Software Intern : 
 Build the software behind the technology. 
 As a System Tools Software Intern , you'll create the software that powers engineering teams and next-generation products. You'll design, develop, test, and improve tools that make systems faster, more reliable, and easier to build.
 In this role, you may:
 Design and develop system software, utilities, and engineering tools.
 Build or enhance operating systems, compilers, networking tools, databases, and Internet-based applications.
 Troubleshoot, debug, and optimize software performance.
 Collaborate with hardware and software engineers to ensure seamless integration.
 Help influence hardware design by developing software that works efficiently with new technologies.
 Applications Software Intern: 
 Create software that helps teams work smarter. 
 As an Applications Software Engineer , you'll develop applications that support employees, customers, and business operations. You'll design, build, test, and improve software used across enterprise systems.
 In this role, you may:
 Design, develop, and maintain commercial and internal software applications.
 Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code using modern programming languages.
 Test, debug, and improve application performance.
 Collaborate with teammates to build new features and solve technical problems.
 Create documentation that supports software deployment and ongoing maintenance.
 Data Analytics Intern : 
 Turn data into insights that drive better decisions. 
 As a Data Analytics Engineer , you'll build the tools and data systems that help teams understand performance, improve products, and solve business challenges. You'll work with large datasets to create meaningful insights that influence engineering and business decisions.
 In this role, you may:
 Design and develop data pipelines, databases, and data warehouses.
 Build software and automation tools for collecting, processing, and analyzing data.
 Create dashboards, reports, and visualizations that support decision-making.
 Partner with stakeholders to understand business needs and translate them into technical solutions.
 Analyze data to identify trends, improve processes, and solve complex problems.
 Firmware Engineering Intern : 
 Write the code that brings hardware to life. 
 As a Firmware Intern , you'll develop the low-level software that allows hardware devices to function. Working at the intersection of hardware and software, you'll help build reliable, high-performance embedded systems used in next-generation technology.
 In this role, you may:
 Design, develop, test, and debug embedded firmware.
 Write software using C, C++, assembly, and other low-level programming languages.
 Collaborate with hardware engineers to integrate software with electronic systems.
 Troubleshoot firmware and hardware interactions to improve performance and reliability.
 Support new product development from concept through production.
 This role is part of WD's early career development program. listings.title: Firmware Engineer Intern - BS - Summer 2027
listings.desc:
About Marvell 
 Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 
 At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 
 Your Team, Your Impact 
Marvell's firmware engineering teams span multiple cutting-edge domains, giving you the opportunity to work on technologies that power next-generation cloud, AI, storage, and networking solutions. Firmware engineers may contribute to secure, high-performance firmware for compute and custom ASIC platforms, embedded software for SSDs, or trusted firmware stacks for hardware security modules. Other teams focus on networking innovation, developing tools and firmware for dynamic services, or creating embedded solutions for high-speed PAM4 DSP chips and optical communication links. Across all groups, you’ll collaborate with hardware and software engineers to deliver robust, scalable solutions that enable Marvell’s leadership in data infrastructure. 
 What You Can Expect 
 As a Firmware Engineer Intern at Marvell, you could:
 Develop and maintain embedded firmware for advanced hardware platforms, including data center, AI devices, SSD controllers, DSP networking chips, and high-speed PAM4 DSPs.
 Design and implement device drivers and firmware features for communication protocols (SPI, I2C, I3C, UART, MDIO, PCIe, NVMe) and RTOS-based systems.
 Participate in full product lifecycle : concept, design, implementation, testing, validation, and release to customers.
 Create and enhance automation scripts (Python, shell, bash) for testing, failure analysis workflows, and infrastructure management.
 Develop provisioning software and trusted firmware stacks to enable advanced security features for SoCs, including cryptography and secure protocols (TLS/SSL, IPSec).
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Hardware, System, QA, Customer Solutions) for integration, debugging, and performance optimization.
 Design and execute unit, system, and integration tests , including regression planning and continuous integration (Jenkins).
 Support lab testing and data analysis , including tool development for debugging, proof-of-concept preparation, and customer documentation.
 Work on mission-critical features for top-tier cloud customers and gain exposure to DSP concepts (Equalizers, Filters) and networking fundamentals (Ethernet, TCP/IP, OSI model).
 Debug complex hardware/software issues , drive root cause analysis, and manage fixes through issue tracking systems (e.g., Jira).
 What We're Looking For 
 Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 and Summer 2028 
 Strong problem-solving, verbal, and written communication skills
 Proficiency in Python and/or C
 Comfortable working in Windows or Linux-based development environments
 Understanding of computer architecture, networking fundamentals (OSI model, TCP/IP), and/or embedded systems
 Knowledge or experience with any of the following technical skills:
 Git, GitHub, or Gerrit
 Linux, Makefiles, GDB, IDEs, and bash scripting
 ARM CPU, RISC-V, TrustZone, Caliptra, or Trusted Firmware
 RTOS architecture, device drivers, and communication protocols (SPI, I2C, I3C, UART, USB, PCIe, MDIO)
 Security protocols (IPSec, TLS/SSL, SPDM, digital certificates, cryptography)
 DSP concepts (Equalizers, Filters, ADC, DAC, FFE, DFE)
 Python/bash scripting, Jenkins CI, and software regression planning
 GUI development, lab automation, and customer SDKs
 Ethernet, SERDES, Switches, and Routers
 Unit testing, system integration

listings.title: Embedded Software Engineer Intern
listings.desc:
Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally?
 About Analog Devices 
 Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com  and on LinkedIn and X .
 At ADI, you will learn from the brightest minds who are here to help you grow and succeed. During your internship, you will make an impact through work on meaningful projects alongside a team of experts. Collaborating with colleagues in an environment of respect and responsibility, you will create connections that will become a part of your professional network.
 ADI’s culture values aligned goals, work-life balance, continuous and life-long learning opportunities, and shared rewards. The internship program features various lunch-and-learn topics and social events with other interns and full-time employees.
 At ADI, our goal is to develop our interns so they are the first to be considered for full-time roles.
 Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.
 About the Role
 As an Embedded Software Engineer Intern, you will gain hands-on experience developing software and firmware for embedded systems that power real-world applications. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will contribute to software design, implementation, testing, and debugging while collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver reliable and efficient embedded solutions.
 Key Responsibilities
 Assist in developing, testing, and debugging embedded software and firmware for hardware-based systems.
 Support the integration of software and hardware components to ensure system functionality and performance.
 Contribute to the development of automation tools, test frameworks, and software utilities.
 Participate in system validation, data collection, and performance analysis activities.
 Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to troubleshoot issues and implement solutions.
 Document software designs, test results, and technical findings.
 Must Have Skills
 Basic knowledge of embedded systems, software development, and computer engineering principles.
 Familiarity with programming languages such as C, C++, Python, or similar languages.
 Understanding of software debugging, testing, and problem-solving techniques.
 Knowledge of version control tools such as Git or similar platforms.
 Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and communication skills.
 Ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.
 Eagerness to learn new technologies, tools, and development methodologies.
 Preferred Education and Experience
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
 Familiarity with embedded operating systems, real-time systems (RTOS), or embedded Linux environments.
 Exposure to software build systems, scripting, or automation tools.
 Experience with engineering projects, coursework, or research involving embedded software, firmware, hardware-software integration, or system validation.
 Knowledge of digital signal processing, communication protocols, or embedded hardware concepts is a plus.

 Job Description: 
 What if your next project helped power the future of technology? 
 At Intel, you'll do more than learn, you'll contribute. You'll work side-by-side with industry leaders, gain hands-on experience on meaningful projects, and help solve real-world challenges that affect billions of people worldwide. From advanced semiconductor manufacturing to AI-powered innovations, you'll play a role in technologies that redefine how the world works, learns, and connects.

 - Contributing to cross domain systems integration and validation work, ensuring vehicle features function correctly end to end

 - Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and debugging sessions with your team

 - Contribute to test automation and validation for integration or connectivity features

 - Document your work and present progress to your team throughout the internship


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university

 - Proficient in at least one of Python, Go, C++, or Java

 - Actively pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship

 - Exposure to distributed systems, event driven architecture, or cloud platforms, AWS preferred

 - Coursework or project experience with backend development, systems integration, or test automation

Candidates should be available from January 11, 2027 to August 13, 2027.

As a Software Engineering Intern, you will support the Infotainment Platform Enablement team focused on next-generation infotainment platforms. The team enables early hardware bring-up develops manufacturing validation software, and builds system-level workload emulation and diagnostics frameworks to de-risk high compute automotive platforms well ahead of production. This role offers hands-on exposure to embedded systems, hardware-software integration, vehicle workload emulation, and large-scale diagnostics telemetry systems running on cutting-edge compute platforms.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Contribute to the design and implementation of a Software Application Framework for infotainment and validation systems

 - Assist in emulating vehicle workloads to validate system behavior and power/performance characteristics

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver scalable solutions

 - Currently enrolled in a full-time degree program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

 - Strong programming skills in C/C++ and/or Python

 - Understanding of embedded systems fundamentals

 - Must be located in Champaign, IL and able to work out of our office in the Research Park.

 - Exposure to embedded platform architecture (GPU, PCIe, camera pipelines, high-speed interfaces)

   - WiFi / Bluetooth / networking interfaces
   
   - Linux-based embedded systems

 - Experience with telemetry, data processing, or analytics tools (e.g., Databricks or equivalent data platforms) is a plus

listings.title: System Test Engineer  Intern
listings.desc:
Who You’ll Work With 
 Arista Networks is looking for world-class Software Test Engineers (aka System Test engineers) to help us in building the highest quality networking products for the AGNI team. 
 Arista Guardian for Network Identity (AGNI) is Arista’s network identity and access management solution. It provides secure authentication, authorization, and visibility for users, devices, and applications accessing the network. AGNI uses a cloud-native, microservices-based architecture and leverages ML/AI to simplify operations, support zero-trust security, and scale with modern enterprise networks. It integrates with existing identity sources and network infrastructure and is available as both a SaaS and on-premises solution.
 If you love networking, working on complex & scaled out network topologies makes you excited and if you like to challenge yourself to find the hard-to-find bugs and if troubleshooting & debugging network and system problems gives you a thrill, this role is tailor made for you.
 At Arista, you’ll bring your intelligence, creativity, and drive every day & work with our products exactly how they are going to be used by our end customers and while doing so, make sure that the products are going to work every time. You will engage with our products as end-users would, ensuring their consistent functionality and reliability. 
 Your job is to find the hard bugs, the ones not easily exposed by the developers’ automated unit and product level tests. You will NOT spend your time running manual regressions of mind numbing, 1000 page test plans, because Arista’s developers automate all the basic functional and integration tests. 
 Courtesy of our super collaborative work environment, you’ll spend your time embedded deeply with multiple engineering teams, working side by side with the developers, POC engineers, account teams, working together as one team and do all of it to help us to explore, find and fix software problems before they can reach the customers. We take quality seriously and we invite you to be a champion of software quality!!
 What You’ll Do 
 Work with the developers in your team in creating their plans for automated tests to complement the exploratory testing that you perform. 
 Participate in functional specification and software design reviews held by your team and provide customer centric input. 
 Work in a highly productive environment along with the best of the engineers on the Linux platform that cuts a typical development cycle by order of magnitude with a laser focus towards quality. 
 Use every means possible to find the bugs in the software and/or hardware being developed by your team. 
 Write test plans to validate Arista features and products. 
 Design test network topologies to validate functionality, performance, stability and scalability of features and products. 
 Execute test plans to verify all aspects of the product. Identify defects and validate resolution. 
 Work as an agile member of a combined development and test team, running in short cycles to develop functional software in quick iterations.
 BS CS/CE/EE plus 1+ years of experience. MS degree preferred 
 Experience in creating test methodologies and writing test plans or System Software skills. 
 Strong knowledge in the following areas: 802.1X, RADIUS, TACACS+, AAA, NAC, VLANs, IP Routing, TCP/IP, L2-L3 protocols. 
 Experience in configuring wired switches and/or wireless access points of different vendors for network access use-cases. 
 Familiarity with Identity Providers like Okta, Microsoft Active Directory, OneLogin are desirable. 
 Desirable to have experience in testing cloud-native SaaS applications ● Experience with working on other AAA or NAC products like ISE and ClearPass are desirable. 
 Good working knowledge of structured programming languages such as Python, Go, C, C++ etc. desirable 
 Strong communication skills.
 Compensation: 
 The intern base pay for this role is $80,000 to $85,000 / year.

listings.desc:
About GlobalFoundries  
 GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GF makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit www.gf.com . 
 Internship Program Overview:   
 Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. 
 Summary of Role:  
 GlobalFoundries has a 2025 Internship Position available at the Malta, NY site for a Production Control Engineer intern. 
 Essential Responsibilities include:  
 As a member of the Production Control team, you will be working on projects that enable solutions driving towards delivering New Product Introduction initiatives at aggressive delivery commits. 
 This role will provide insight into the business processes that are involved in securing future business for the fab and the close-knit coordination between Customer Engineering, Integration, Planning, and Line control to ensure successful New Product Introduction in a timely manner. 
 This position is for a candidate that will graduate and be ready to enter the workforce within the next year. This candidate must be enrolled in a BS/MS in Industrial Engineering, Computer Science / Data Science or another relevant engineering discipline. 
 Successful candidates will be comfortable leading improvement projects and working on a diverse team in a manufacturing environment. They will work in a dynamic collaborative environment requiring strong teaming skills with engineers, managers, technicians and production employees. 
 Other Responsibilities:  
 Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. 
 Required Qualifications:  
 Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s in Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship.  
 Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing. 
 Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal)  
 Ability to work at least  40 hours per week during the internship.  
 Preferred Qualifications:   
 Prior related internship or co-op experience 
 Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc. 
 Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity.  
 Strong written and verbal communication skills  
 Strong planning & organizational skills 
 Experience implementing productivity/efficiency improvements and working knowledge factory automation 
 IT skills to support data analysis and reporting

 Project management skills

 Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship.

 Prior related internship or co-op experience

Who We Are  
 Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.
Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.
With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.
Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.
 About the Role 
 As a software engineering intern, you will work closely with leading experts in the field of machine learning, robotics, and software. Depending on your skill sets and areas of interest, you will work on some or all of the following: Data Platform, Onboard Systems, ML Infrastructure, Simulation, or Technical Infrastructure teams.
 About the Work 
 Depending on your skill set and areas of interest you will work on some or all of the following:
 Data Platform: The Data Platform serves as a comprehensive management system for Nuro AI Driver's data, labels, and metrics, facilitating seamless access functionality. The team focuses on data annotation across various domains, including 2D/3D perception, mapping, behavior trajectory, and language/text. It also handles data ingestion and mining, employing methods such as heuristics and embedding search. Additionally, the platform supports the autonomy evaluation infrastructure by providing detailed introspection. 
 Onboard Systems: Our onboard system team’s software engineers provide a reliable and high-performance platform that allows our autonomy teams to integrate their autonomy software and algorithms that work across various self-driving platforms. This work requires close collaboration with our software teams, hardware teams, and systems/safety team to make sure new software and hardware work together safely and reliably and resolve onboard error and performance problems.
 ML Infrastructure: The ML Infra team is the accelerator to our ML-first autonomy strategy. This team provides solutions to empower machine learning development in Nuro and optimize on-cloud training and onboard inference. Our solutions include a distributed training platform, ML compiler, model components libraries, e.t.c. The team provides opportunities for infra engineers to work fully embedded in ML teams to build cutting edge deep learning technologies.
 Simulation: The Simulation team builds the simulator that allows us to develop and test our autonomous driving technology in a virtual setting. We work on the core simulator and simulation frameworks, sensor simulation, scenario generation, and solutions that combine real-world data with synthetic techniques to push the boundaries of what can be simulated, collaborating closely with teams across Autonomy and AI Platform to allow us to simulate realistically and reliably at scale.
 Technical Infrastructure: this group owns few fundamental services for entire engineering organizations: generic compute platform to host mission-critical workflows such as data processing and simulation, storage management service which manages hundreds of PB of data, cloud infrastructure serves as IaaC which provisions and maintains all cloud resources, engineering productivity provides tools such as build and CI/CD to make engineering work more efficient.

 Join the Skyworks San Jose Design Center in developing high-performance silicon RFIC solutions for next-generation mobile applications. This internship offers hands-on experience in silicon RFIC design while working closely with experienced engineers in a collaborative team environment.

The work will focus on transistor-level circuit design, simulation, layout, and laboratory evaluation of high-performance RF front-end circuits. The intern will also document results and present technical work to colleagues and stakeholders.

 •  Experience with RF test equipment, including network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, DC power supplies, and RF probes.

listings.title: 2027 Summer Intern, BS/MS, Embedded, Software Engineer
listings.desc:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.
 Software Engineering in the Hardware organization is where software meets the physical world. The Waymo Embedded Software Engineering team develops the critical, safety-critical software running at the edge of the Waymo driver, interfacing directly with steering, braking, propulsion, power distribution, and vehicle sensors. You will develop the abstractions and business logic to safely control and manage autonomous vehicles across different vehicle platforms and OEMs. Operating under stringent real-time, deterministic, and fail-operational constraints, the team builds high-reliability onboard firmware and off-vehicle simulation tooling, having a direct and material impact on Waymo's ability to scale safely to more vehicles and cities.
 Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!
 You will: 
 Develop high-quality vertically-integrated C++ software systems (on-vehicle firmware and off-vehicle simulation/tooling) running at the edge of the Waymo driver.               
 Contribute directly to the bring-up, validation, and debugging of next-generation compute platforms, peripheral drivers, and hardware-software interfaces for new vehicle platforms.                                                                                                                  
 Write robust unit tests (such as gTest) and Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) simulation fixtures to validate edge-case handling, system robustness, and fault containment.                                                                                                                                           
 Analyze field data logs, vehicle telemetry, and simulation results to identify root causes and improve firmware performance. 
 Participate in cross-functional engineering workflows, design discussions, and code reviews alongside experienced embedded and systems engineers. 
 You have: 
 Enrolled in a BS or MS program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field.
 Strong programming foundation in C or C++, with a solid understanding of  data structures, pointers, and memory management.                          
 High curiosity, a continuous learning mindset, and the enthusiasm to explore unfamiliar hardware architectures, tools, and codebases.           
 Demonstrated problem-solving ability, debugging skills, and comfort navigating ambiguity when working with evolving platforms or prototypes.   
 Familiarity with Linux development environments, command-line tools, and version control systems (e.g., Git).
 We prefer: 
 Embedded Systems and Real-Time Programming: Hands-on experience developing software for microcontrollers (such as ARM Cortex-M or Cortex-R), bare-metal environments, or RTOS with resource-constrained execution.                                           
 Hardware Bring-Up and Lab Debugging: Practical experience with board bring-up, hardware-software integration, and lab instrumentation such as oscillo

listings.desc: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers. Responsibilities As a research intern in Keysight's Advanced Technology Laboratories, you will work on photonic integrated circuit (PIC) characterization and analysis using automated state-of-the-art instrumentation in a well-equipped laboratory. You will have an opportunity to investigate PICs with a variety of functionalities for atypical applications with challenging requirements. You will be expected to help improve and further automate existing PIC characterization tools and analysis methodologies to increase productivity and reveal new insights. Hands-on experience characterizing PICs will be a key attribute of a successful candidate. In addition, the work might include simulation and design to improve existing integrated components and circuits or to create new ones. You will be working with a talented and multi-disciplinary team in Keysight’s central research laboratory uniquely chartered with inventing and developing breakthrough electronic and photonic measurement technologies. With your skills and experience and an intern position in Keysight Labs, you will contribute directly to the revolution in photonic integration. If your project is successful, you may see the results of your work in next-generation products from Keysight. This position requires hands-on laboratory work and close collaboration with other team members. Consequently, this job must be performed from our offices in Santa Clara, California. Qualifications The successful candidate will possess a theoretical understanding and practical skills in photonic integrated circuits (PICs). Job Requirements: Completed a B.S. degree in an engineering or science discipline Graduate student* majoring in Optics, Photonics, Physics, or Electrical Engineering Strong familiarity with PICs including: Integrated waveguide types and their properties Common fiber-to-chip coupling techniques and related components (optical I/O) Passive components (directional couplers, polarization splitters, rings, MMI’s, etc.) Active components (photodetectors, modulators, heaters, lasers, etc.) Hands-on experience with both optical and electrical test and measurement instrumentation Python programming skills and familiarity with engineering packages (Numpy, Matplotlib, etc.) Experience in PIC component simulation, modeling and design Strong written and verbal English communication skills Self-motivated with an ability to work collaboratively in a multi-disciplinary team Other valuable skills: Lab automation – instrument control, data acquisition and motion control Familiarity with integrated photonic chip handling techniques Experience in PIC layout and GDS file handling Noise and signal analysis experience Familiarity with inverse design, agentic design, or data analytics California Salary Range: MIN $63.53 - MAX $68.41 *Candidates who wish to be considered must be enrolled in an accredited college/university as of September 2027. Applicants who are graduating before September 2027 will not be considered unless they are entering/applying to a MS or PHD program after graduating. Visa Sponsorship is not available for this position. Candidates who now or at any point in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B Visa status) may not be considered. listings.title: Software Architecture Engineer Intern
listings.desc:
AI Vision Processors For Edge Applications 
 Our solutions make cameras smarter by extracting valuable data from high-resolution video streams. 
 Job Description 
 Ambarella has some exciting internship opportunities for self-motivated and creative students near completing of their master's degree.   We are looking for talented software programmers who possess a strong interest in computer architecture, VLSI design, image processing, video compression, and computer vision.
 Architecture interns study hardware and software trade-offs present in the latest version of our chips and explore uses of both to solve real-world problems.  Interns may develop software models of important behaviors in hardware co-processors such as memory bandwidth and pipeline latency or develop visualization tools to illustrate architecture behavior.  Interns produce support tools to enable software to make efficient use of hardware co-processors.   A final presentation at the end of the internships describes their findings and allows other team members to use their work for ongoing projects.
 The internship program requires experience in modern programming languages and computer architecture. C++, C, Python, and CUDA are our popular tools.  Exposure to common neural networks frameworks such as PyTorch helps.  We expect that interns will be able to pick up missing skills quickly, deliver their assignments on time, and present their work at the end of the program.

listings.title: Software Engineer Intern 2026/2027
listings.desc:
Who you'll work with 
 Arista Networks is looking for Graduate Engineers interested in learning world leading product development in C/C++, Go and other languages. Join us at Arista Networks advancing the Software Defined Networking (SDN) revolution. 
 What You’ll Do  
 Writing Linux user space and kernel code to allow 32-bit drivers to DMA 64-bit virtual memory spaces using both Intel and AMD IOMMU controller.
 Working on the hardware/software boundary for chips and the kernel. Where an x86 chip might have tens of registers, you will routinely work on ASICs with thousands of registers, tables, and special TCAM memories. You will program networking chips to provide latency analysis and keep accurate counts of events happening billions of times per second. You will write Python to bootstrap new hardware. You will build software agents that mediate and translate between the requirements of switching ASICs, high capacity custom FPGAs, media adapters, and PCIe bridges. You might tune lasers and measure and correct error rates measured in parts per billion. 
 Implementing communications protocols between routers and switches at layer 2 (such as LLDP, 802.1x, BFD, etc), and layer 3 (such as BGP, OSPF, ISIS).
 Updating the forwarding state of the hardware, using platform-independent abstractions.
 Reconciling the linux kernel routing model with the switch's forwarding state.
 Implementing a policy language used for filtering and manipulating routing data received and advertised to peers
 Accessing ASIC registers over SPI bus, SMbus, PCIe and I2C, to implement high resolution timers (sub-100ns accuracy) and read ASIC hardware specifications to gather near-real-time information on large numbers of packet flows and to generate network congestion statistics.
 Developing configuration management services using Go and Python to support YANG, OpenConfig, NETCONF and RESTCONF over gRPC, ssh and ssl for standardised switch configuration, combined with tools such as git, gerrit, Jenkins, Slack and Trello.
 Developing routing protocol agents (for BGP, OSPF, ISIS) in C/C++ within a Fedora Linux embedded environment. Coding of fault-tolerant, concurrent agents capable of handling the demands of future data centres where high performance and high availability are basic requirements. Fully automated, developer owned, Python based, continuous test harness with 100s of devices under test at any one moment.
 #LI-EO1
 Any of the following:- C, C++, Java, Python, Go, react.js, redux.js, node.js Networking, Linux Embedded Systems, Algorithms, Programming, Software Development.

listings.title: Co-Op, (Manufacturing Software Development)
listings.desc:
JOB DESCRIPTION 
 This position is for Undergraduate and Graduate Students 
 Co-op Cycle: January 4th to June 25th, 2027
 Schedule: Monday- Friday 8:00am to 4:30pm
 Location: Beverly, MA (Onsite)
 *To support students commuting to our Beverly, MA facility, we offer a travel stipend. See the Commute section below.
 Ready to turn what you’re learning in the classroom into real-world impact? 
 Axcelis is a global leader in ion implantation and semiconductor technology. Our co‑ops don’t just observe—they contribute . For more than four decades, we’ve been driving innovation in semiconductor manufacturing technology, working with the world’s leading chipmakers to power everything from smartphones to electric vehicles. As a co‑op, you’ll gain hands‑on experience , learn from industry experts, and make a real impact on projects that shape the future of technology.
 We are searching for our next group of engineering co-ops for a 6-month assignment at our Beverly, MA, facility. Our co‑op program is designed to develop early‑career talent and build a strong pipeline of future engineers . Students gain hands-on exposure , work on real projects , and make meaningful contributions . Throughout the program, co‑ops build technical skills , strengthen problem‑solving abilities , and gain real‑world experience that enhances both their academic learning and future career opportunities.
 About the Role 
 Axcelis is seeking a Manufacturing Software Engineering Co-op to support our Operations Technology team in business system integration, custom applications, and operational analysis and optimization. This role offers hands-on experience at the intersection of manufacturing, technology, and data-driven decision-making.
 The ideal candidate is an engineering student with software experience who is eager to apply their skills in a manufacturing and operations-focused environment.
 What You’ll Do 
 Assist in developing and maintaining ERP integrations with manufacturing systems.
 Support the development of custom applications to streamline operations.
 Analyze operational data and contribute to process optimization initiatives.
 Work closely with engineering, production, and IT teams to solve real-world manufacturing challenges.
 Document findings and provide recommendations for efficiency improvements.
 What We’re Looking For 
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related field.
 Experience with database setup and integration (MSSQL).
 Interest in manufacturing operations, process improvement, and technology integration.
 Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
 Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
 Preferred Qualifications: Proficiency in Python and JavaScript Node for application development and deployment.
 Experience with C#, .NET
 Experience with databases (SQL)
 Familiarity with REST APIs and ERP systems.
 Understanding of data visualization and analysis techniques.
 Why Choose Axcelis for Your Co-op? 
 Meaningful Work – Work on real projects that make a direct impact on our products, processes, and customers
 Leadership That Knows Your Name – Senior leaders are invested in our Co-ops’ growth and regularly engage with students throughout their assignment.
 Mentorship – Co-ops are matched with an experienced mentor to help them navigate the company, build connections, and succeed in their role.
 More Than a Co-op – Our co-op program is a key pipeline for full-time early career roles, giving you a strong starting point after graduation.
 Engaging Co-op Experience : Enjoy off-site co-op events, weekly co-op meetups, and company-hosted luncheons that help you learn, network, and feel part of the Axcelis team.
 This co-op provides real-world experience in a manufacturing environment where technology meets operations. If you’re passionate about solving complex problems and optimizing industrial workflows, apply today!

At Cadence, we hire and develop leaders and innovators who want to make an impact on the world of technology. 
 Cadence Design Systems is a pivotal leader in electronic design, building upon more than 30 years of computational software expertise. The company applies its underlying Intelligent System Design strategy to deliver software, hardware and IP that turn design concepts into reality. Cadence customers are the world’s most innovative companies, delivering extraordinary electronic products from chips & boards to systems for the most dynamic market applications including consumer, hyperscale computing, 5G communications, automotive, aerospace industrial and health. 
 Cadence Ireland is entering an exciting time – we are building a new R&D Centre of Excellence here in Cork. At the IP Group (IPG) we are building world-class high-speed communication and memory IC (Integrated Circuit) products for applications in datacentre SoC processors as well as in consumer, industrial and automotive electronics. Cadence focus on the leading-edge CMOS geometry nodes such as e.g., 5nm TSMC. 
 Of course, we also have everything else you would expect from a world class technology organization & fortune 100 company, ranked as one of the best places to work worldwide. 
 https://fortune.com/best-companies/2020/cadence 
 We are hiring and looking for interns. If you are passionate about technology and love to learn, work and grow in a multi geography and multi culture organization developing next generation technologies, you should apply as per below:

 Location:                                             Galway

 This Internship will introduce you the basics skills of analog and digital IC design for high-speed communication circuits (e.g. 112 Gbps) used in data centre and cloud applications. You will also participate in team meetings and learn firsthand how an industry design team builds the world’s fastest CMOS communication ICs.

listings.title: 2H University Intern - Implant Process Engineering
listings.desc:
About GlobalFoundries  
 GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GF makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit  www.gf.com . 
 Internship Program Overview:   
 Our Interns are our talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you will experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. 
 Project Title: 
 Implant Process Engineering
 Project Objective: 
 To d evelop robust, high-volume manufacturable protocols for phosphorus-to-arsenic surface cleaning and conversion to mitigate phosphorus cross-contamination in arsenic-doped semiconductor wafers. 
 Project Outcome:  
 The intern will gain comprehensive exposure to semiconductor fabrication operations, with a focus on advanced ion implantation process engineering and fundamental equipment handling. Training will include application of PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) methodology for continuous improvement. 
 Additionally, the intern will be introduced to failure analysis techniques such as Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (SIMS) and data analytics using JMP software. 
 The project will require the intern to perform cost-benefit and productivity impact assessments for proposed process solutions.

 Your Team, Your Impact 
The Power Design team is responsible for driving power efficiency throughout the chip design lifecycle, from early architecture and RTL through physical implementation and final signoff.
The team develops and owns the methodologies, tools, and flows used to estimate, analyze, track, and optimize chip power. We work closely with architecture, RTL, verification, and physical design teams to identify power challenges early, understand their root causes, and drive effective solutions while balancing power, performance, and area (PPA).
Our work includes developing power models and estimation capabilities, analyzing power at different stages of the design flow, identifying optimization opportunities, and driving improvements at both the RTL and physical design levels. The team also explores new automation and AI-based methodologies to make power analysis faster, more accurate, and more actionable.
As the chip’s power center of expertise, the team provides technical guidance, establishes best practices, tracks power targets, and drives power-related activities across the broader chip design organization. 
 What You Can Expect 
 Ramp up on chip power estimation methodologies, tools, and power calculators.
 Perform power analysis and identify optimization opportunities throughout the chip design lifecycle.
 Explore and implement power optimizations at both the RTL and physical design levels .
 Develop automation and improve existing power analysis and estimation flows.
 Explore the use of AI tools for power analysis, optimization, and design-flow automation .
 Analyze power trends and identify high-impact areas for improvement.
 Collaborate with RTL, physical design, architecture, and power teams to drive power-related activities.
 Gradually become a power focal point within the chip design team , building expertise and ownership of power methodologies, analysis, and optimization.
 What We're Looking For 
 To be successful in this role, you must:
- at least 2nd year student for Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or similar field.
- Have coursework relating to foundational principles of circuit design, circuit theory, digital logic design, or electronics.
